title: Kubernetes for ML Services
interviewAnswer: Kubernetes schedules containers across a cluster and provides deployments, services, scaling and rolling updates. Use it when operational complexity and scale justify the platform overhead.
why: Kubernetes matters when ML services need replicated deployment, scheduling, service discovery and controlled rollouts across clusters.
intuition: You declare the desired state—such as three replicas of an inference container—and Kubernetes continuously tries to make the cluster match it.
deepDive: Pods are the basic scheduling unit; Deployments manage stateless replicas/rollouts; Services provide stable networking; ConfigMaps/Secrets inject config; persistent volumes handle durable storage. Readiness controls traffic; liveness detects stuck processes. GPU workloads require node/device scheduling. Kubernetes adds significant operational complexity and is unnecessary for every project.
workedExample: An inference Deployment runs three API pods behind a Service; a readiness probe prevents a pod receiving traffic until the model checkpoint is loaded.
code: # concept: Deployment -> ReplicaSet -> Pods; Service routes to ready Pods
commonMistakes: Calling a container and pod the same thing.
Using liveness checks that restart healthy but slow model-loading pods.
Choosing Kubernetes for a single simple batch job without need.
production: Define resource requests/limits, autoscaling signals, disruption/rollout policies and model warmup behavior; managed container services may be simpler when cluster control is unnecessary.
